Stated Claim / Post Context:
Kid Rock details sit-down with Trump, Stephen A Smith and Bill Maher

Kid Rock revealed details from an "epic" White House dinner with President Donald Trump, Bill Maher and Stephen A. Smith where socialism and HBCUs took center stage.

Actual Article Body:

Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Singer Kid Rock joins 'Fox & Friends' to discuss his White House dinner with President Trump, comedian Bill Maher and ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, the high-stakes Michigan Senate race and his new album, ‘Halfway 2 Jesus.’

Kid Rock joined "Fox & Friends" Friday and said he recently had dinner with President Donald Trump, comedian Bill Maher and ESPN host Stephen A. Smith.

After talking about the Michigan Senate race and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Kid Rock told the hosts of "Fox & Friends" there was one thing he, Maher, Smith and Trump all agreed on.

"Last night, I'm having dinner at the White House with the president, Bill Maher and Stephen A. Smith. We all agreed socialism and communism has no place to have a foothold in our government," he said, before referring to El-Sayed.

"This guy is screaming socialism."

UNEARTHED SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS CONTRADICT EL-SAYED’S ‘CAPITALIST’ NARRATIVE

Musician Kid Rock arrives to speak during a rally with President Donald Trump at F&M Bank Arena in Clarksville, Tenn., Oct. 10, 2026. (Getty Images)

Asked how the dinner went, Kid Rock said the group had a great conversation.

"It was epic," he said. "And the thing that was the greatest, there's so many points, I could do an hour on it, is that, you know, two Democrats, two Republicans sit down, break bread, have laughs, talk about, have tough conversations on a lot of the issues."

The musician described some of the issues Maher and Smith raised with Trump.

"Everything from socialism and communism to the war in Iran to Bill Maher was talking getting our interpreters and things from Afghanistan that helped us out," he said.

"Stephen A. Smith was very much engaged in talking about unemployment with Black women and the funding of HBCUs, which we reminded him that President Trump did fund $174 million to historically Black universities and colleges in 2016 [sic], which was great."

TRUMP IS DISMANTLING IRAN’S WAR MACHINE, BUT AMERICA STILL NEEDS AN ENDGAME

Stephen A. Smith speaks on stage as he and Christopher Russo host SiriusXM shows live from Fanatics Fest at Javits Center July 17, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images for SiriusXM)

Kid Rock said Smith made the point that, "With Trump putting a dagger through the heart of DEI, it seems like it's scared off a lot of corporate money coming to HBCUs.

"I want to make the point. I'll go out on a limb and say I’m speaking for President Trump and the administration saying, no, no, not only do we support, we want to encourage corporations to continue funding HBCUs and donating to them. We know how important education is, especially in the Black community, to strengthen Black families," he added.

Maher and Kid Rock previously had dinner with Trump at the White House in 2025. Maher recently revealed that he planned to meet with the president again.

"I'm having dinner with him again next week," Maher told famed Hollywood agent and executive Ari Emanuel during a conversation on Maher's "Club Random" podcast.

MAHER MOCKS LIBERALS FOR STILL PANICKING ABOUT TRUMP'S ANTICS, PERSONALITY AFTER 10 YEARS

"After the first dinner, I went back to doing what I do. ... But then, like, he just, out of the blue, 'Let's have dinner again.' And I was like, ‘Great.’ And he was really nice," Maher said.

"Like, 'I promise I won't say bad things about you like I did the last time.' And I texted back, and I said, 'You know what, you're the president of the United States. Say whatever the f--- you want. I'm just glad we're talking.' It's like being called a 'hockey puck' by Don Rickles. It's just what he does. It's how he talks."

Kid Rock also spoke to "Outnumbered" on Friday about his new album, "Halfway 2 Jesus," which includes collaborations with Eminem and Lil Wayne, among others.

"Not just me and my old friend of nearly 40 years, Eminem. Lil Wayne came on last minute," Kid Rock said, "Because me and Eminem decided a different song we did was more powerful than the other one we did, so it left a void there. And Lil Wayne, just being the ace he is. I mean, just, as solid as human beings come."

PRESIDENT TALKS 'TRUMP OCEAN,' TRADES JOKES WITH TENNESSEE CROWD AS KID ROCK KICKS OFF SPRAWLING RALLY

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The singer said he had voices of all kinds of different backgrounds and political beliefs on the album.

"I told him, I go, ‘Wayne, whatever you need me for, I will always be there,’" Kid Rock said. "'If you need to come change your tires, I'll be there to rotate them, whatever.' But not only them, and the other guests on the record, Gary LaVox and Jimmy Allen, but all the musicians, the songwriters, engineers, we are all from different backgrounds, different religions, different political beliefs.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"And yet we came together to make this powerful, very beautiful piece of work that — I haven't promoted many records in the last 10, 15 years — but very important to promote this one because I'm promoting the message of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. And that's bigger than me."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

Disturbing new details emerge about California cop killer who slaughtered wife and daughter: ‘Monster’

A retired San Francisco police sergeant who gunned down his wife and daughter before turning the gun on himself was in the throes of a bizarre late-life makeover — as a a family friend said he had "a monster inside him."

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A retired San Francisco police sergeant who gunned down his wife and daughter before turning the gun on himself was in the throes of a bizarre late-life makeover — as a a family friend said he had “a monster inside him.”

Kevin Mannix, 68, had reportedly been hitting the gym, shedding pounds and overhauling his appearance as his marriage to former San Francisco Deputy Police Chief Ann Mannix, 65, crumbled.

“He had wanted to chase youth,” Mary Conde, a longtime close friend of Ann, told the San Francisco Chronicle. “It seems like he was on a campaign to revamp his appearance.”

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

Conde described the former police sergeant as being in the middle of a late “midlife crisis” as the couple headed toward divorce.

But the most chilling revelation came when Conde described the darkness she now believes was lurking beneath Kevin’s seemingly ordinary exterior.

“Kevin had a monster inside of him that he was able to suppress for all of his lifetime until Sunday, and that monster came out in the most horrific possible way,” Conde told the Chronicle “And nobody suspected that that was ever a possibility.”

The disturbing comments come after investigators said Kevin fatally shot his wife and their 24-year-old daughter, Katie, inside the family’s home in the affluent Marin County community of Strawberry, east of Mill Valley, on Sunday evening.

He then apparently turned the gun on himself, authorities said.

At least one person managed to escape the house and call 911 as the horror unfolded. The caller reported that Kevin had been drinking red wine, according to investigators.

Authorities have not publicly identified a motive for the suspected double murder-suicide.

Conde, a local entertainment executive who had known Ann for decades, said the shocking violence blindsided those closest to the family.

Still, she admitted that after processing the horrific news, she couldn’t completely dismiss the possibility that Kevin was capable of such brutality.

“I didn’t clutch my pearls and say, ‘Kevin? No way,’” she told the Chronicle.

Meanwhile, newly uncovered records reveal Kevin was still working part-time for the San Francisco Police Department despite retiring from the force in 2018 after 27 years of service.

He had apparently been helping investigate prospective police recruits in the department’s staff services division before being abruptly reassigned to the property division on Sept. 1.

California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedInCalifornia Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, XCalifornia Post  Opinion California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!California Post App: Download here!Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!

The transfer was made at the request of the deputy chief of administration, although the reason behind the move remains unclear.

Department officials declined to comment on the reassignment, according to the Chronicle.

Ann, who had also returned to the department as a part-time employee following her retirement, was a celebrated trailblazer who became the first woman to serve on San Francisco’s SWAT team and eventually command the elite unit.

She later rose to deputy chief, overseeing the department’s Field Operations and Special Operations bureaus. Her brutal death, along with that of her young daughter, has devastated former colleagues and loved ones.

One close friend, who said she had known Ann for decades, previously told thr California Post: “This is so sad for me. She was my best friend of 60 years. Love her, she didn’t deserve this.”

The San Francisco Police Officers Association described the suspected murder-suicide as a “horrific and senseless” tragedy that left the department reeling.

“There are no words that can fully capture the depth of this tragedy, nor are there simple answers to the painful questions we are all asking,” the association said.
